segments.text: Euclid's Elements, Book One, Proposition Thirty-Seven. Triangles on the same base and in the same parallels are equal in area. Let triangles A B C and D B C stand on the same base B C and lie between the same parallel lines A D and B C. We prove that triangle A B C is equal in area to triangle D B C.

segments.text: Then each of the figures E B C A and D B C F is a parallelogram on the same base B C and between the same parallels B C and E F. By Proposition Thirty-Five, parallelogram E B C A is equal in area to parallelogram D B C F. By Proposition Thirty-Four, the diagonal A B bisects parallelogram E B C A, so triangle A B C is half of parallelogram E B C A. Likewise, the diagonal D C bisects parallelogram D B C F, so triangle D B C is half of parallelogram D B C F. Since the halves of equal things are equal to one another, triangle A B C is equal in area to triangle D B C, as was required to prove.
